title: Evolution
syllabus: Origin of life; Biological evolution and evidences for biological evolution from paleontology, comparative anatomy, embryology, and molecular evidence; Darwin's contribution, Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution; Mechanism of evolution - Variation (Mutation and Recombination) and Natural Selection with examples, types of natural selection; Gene flow and genetic drift; Hardy-Weinberg's principle; Adaptive Radiation; Human evolution.

questions.question: In 1953, S.L. Miller created primitive Earth conditions in a laboratory flask. Which gas mixture was subjected to electric discharge at $800^\circ\text{C}$ in his spark-discharge apparatus?
questions.solution: Stanley Miller created electric discharge in a closed flask containing methane ($\text{CH}_4$), hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$), ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$), and water vapour at $800^\circ\text{C}$, resulting in the abiotic synthesis of amino acids (like glycine, alanine, and aspartic acid).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the landmark theories and experiments on the origin of life:

List-I (Scientist / Hypothesis)List-II (Concept / Finding)
(A) Louis Pasteur(I) Chemical evolution (first form of life originated from non-living organic molecules)
(B) Oparin and Haldane(II) Disproved spontaneous generation using swan-necked flask experiment
(C) Theory of Panspermia / Cosmozoic(III) Units of life called spores were transferred to Earth from outer space
(D) Ernst Haeckel(IV) Biogenetic law (Ontogeny recapitulates Phylogeny)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Louis Pasteur disproved spontaneous generation using swan-necked flasks; Oparin (Russia) and Haldane (England) proposed chemical evolution; Panspermia postulated that spores came from meteorites/space; Ernst Haeckel proposed that ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny (later disapproved by Karl Ernst von Baer).

questions.question: Homologous organs provide anatomical evidence for evolution because they possess:
options: Same fundamental anatomical structure and embryonic origin, but perform different functions (divergent evolution)
Different anatomical structure and origin, but perform similar functions (convergent evolution)
Complete absence of functional use in modern descendants
Identical nucleotide sequences in all taxa
questions.solution: Homologous organs share the same basic structural plan and origin, but develop along different directions due to adaptations to different needs (divergent evolution). Examples include forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs, and humans, and thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of structures represents an example of ANALOGOUS organs (convergent evolution)?
options: Sweet potato (root modification) and Potato (stem modification)
Forelimbs of Whale and Forelimbs of Cheetah
questions.solution: Sweet potato (root modification) and potato (stem modification) are analogous structures: both store food (same function) but have different anatomical origins. Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita, forelimbs of mammals, and vertebrate hearts/brains are homologous.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding evolutionary patterns and examples:

List-I (Evolutionary Phenomenon)List-II (Example)
(A) Divergent evolution(I) Eye of Octopus and Eye of Mammals
(B) Convergent evolution(II) Darwin's Finches in Galápagos Islands
(C) Adaptive radiation(III) Forelimbs of Whales, Bats, Cheetah, and Human
(D) Industrial melanism(IV) Biston betularia (peppered moth) in England

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Divergent evolution: Mammalian forelimbs; Convergent evolution: Eyes of octopus and mammals, flippers of penguins and dolphins; Adaptive radiation: Darwin's finches and Australian marsupials; Industrial melanism: Biston betularia.

questions.question: The observation of Industrial Melanism in the peppered moth (Biston betularia) in England after industrialization demonstrated that:
options: Melanic (dark-winged) moths had a selective survival advantage against soot-covered tree trunks, increasing in frequency via natural selection
Pollution caused directed mutations converting white moths into dark moths
Lichens grew abundantly in industrial areas to hide dark moths
White moths transformed into dark moths by acquiring acquired characters
questions.solution: Before industrialisation, white-winged moths were camouflaged by lichens on trees. After industrialisation, tree trunks became dark with soot; dark-winged (melanic) moths were camouflaged and survived predation, demonstrating natural selection of pre-existing variants.

questions.question: Excessive use of chemical herbicides, pesticides, and antibiotics has resulted in the rapid evolution of resistant varieties in a few months/years. This evolution is driven by:
questions.solution: Evolution of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and pesticide-resistant insects is an example of natural selection brought about by anthropogenic action (human intervention).

questions.question: Adaptive Radiation is defined as the evolutionary process in which:
options: Different species evolve from a common ancestor starting from a geographical area and radiating to other habitats (e.g., Darwin's finches)
Unrelated organisms develop similar adaptations due to common ecological pressures
A single species undergoes large-scale polyploidy
Mutations occur randomly without any selective pressure
questions.solution: The process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other geographical areas (habitats) is called adaptive radiation (e.g., Darwin's finches and Australian marsupials).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the evolutionary convergence between Australian Marsupials and Placental Mammals:

List-I (Placental Mammal)List-II (Convergent Australian Marsupial)
(A) Anteater(I) Tasmanian wolf
(B) Flying squirrel(II) Numbat (Banded anteater)
(C) Bobcat(III) Sugar glider (Marsupial flying phalanger)
(D) Wolf(IV) Tasmanian tiger cat

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Anteater $\leftrightarrow$ Numbat; Flying squirrel $\leftrightarrow$ Flying phalanger (Sugar glider); Bobcat $\leftrightarrow$ Tasmanian tiger cat; Wolf $\leftrightarrow$ Tasmanian wolf.

questions.question: According to Hugo de Vries (Mutation Theory), evolution is driven by mutations which are:
options: Random and directionless, causing speciation by single-step large mutations (Saltation)
Small, directional, and continuous as proposed by Darwin
questions.solution: Hugo de Vries believed that mutation caused evolution and not the minor heritable variations that Darwin talked about. Mutations are random and directionless, whereas Darwinian variations are small and directional. De Vries called speciation by single-step large mutation 'saltation'.

questions.question: The Hardy-Weinberg Principle states that allele frequencies in a population are stable and remain constant from generation to generation in the absence of evolutionary influences. It is algebraically expressed as:
questions.solution: The Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium equation is $(p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$, where $p^2$ is the frequency of homozygous dominant individuals ($AA$), $2pq$ is the frequency of heterozygous individuals ($Aa$), and $q^2$ is the frequency of homozygous recessive individuals ($aa$).

questions.question: In a population under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of a recessive allele ($a$) is $0.4$. What is the expected percentage of heterozygous individuals ($Aa$) in this population?
questions.solution: Given $q = 0.4$. Since $p + q = 1$, $p = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$. The frequency of heterozygous individuals ($2pq$) is $2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48 = 48\%$.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Natural Selection and their impact on phenotypic distribution curves:

List-I (Type of Natural Selection)List-II (Effect on Distribution Curve)
(A) Stabilising selection(I) Peak shifts in one specific direction (favours one extreme phenotype)
(B) Directional selection(II) Two distinct peaks form at extremes (favours both peripheral character values)
(C) Disruptive selection(III) Peak gets higher and narrower (favours mean character value)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Stabilising selection favours intermediate phenotypes and narrows the peak; Directional selection shifts the peak toward one extreme; Disruptive selection favours both extreme phenotypes, splitting the curve into two peaks.

questions.question: When a small fraction of an original population migrates to a new geographical location, becomes isolated, and establishes a new population with drastically different allele frequencies, this phenomenon is termed:
options: Founder Effect (a manifestation of Genetic Drift)
questions.solution: When a small group becomes separated from a larger population, the change in allele frequency may be so different in the new sample that they become a different species. The original drifted population becomes founders and the effect is called the Founder effect (a form of genetic drift).

questions.question: In 1938, a live specimen of a lobe-finned fish (Coelacanth / Latimeria) was caught in South Africa. Coelacanths are evolutionary precursors of the first:
questions.solution: In 1938, a fish caught in South Africa happened to be a Coelacanth (lobefin), thought to be extinct. These lobefin fishes evolved into the first amphibians that lived on both land and in water.

questions.question: About 65 million years ago (mya), the dinosaurs suddenly disappeared from the Earth. Which of the following is considered the largest carnivorous terrestrial dinosaur that stood about $20\text{ feet}$ in height and had dagger-like teeth?
questions.solution: About 65 mya, the dinosaurs suddenly disappeared. The biggest terrestrial dinosaur was Tyrannosaurus rex, which stood about 20 feet tall and had fearsome dagger-like teeth.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the stages in Human Evolution and their characteristic cranial capacities:

List-I (Hominid Ancestor)List-II (Cranial Capacity / Key Feature)
(A) Homo habilis(I) $900\text{ cc}$; ate meat, used fire
(B) Homo erectus(II) $650 - 800\text{ cc}$; first human-like tool maker; did not eat meat
(C) Neanderthal man(III) $1400\text{ cc}$; lived in near East/Central Asia; buried their dead
(D) Australopithecus(IV) Walked nearly upright in East African grasslands; hunted with stone weapons; fruit eater

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Homo habilis: $650-800\text{ cc}$ (first hominid, did not eat meat); Homo erectus: $\sim 900\text{ cc}$ (ate meat); Neanderthal: $1400\text{ cc}$ (used hides, buried dead); Australopithecus: lived in East Africa, fruit eater, brain capacity $< 600\text{ cc}$.

questions.question: About 15 million years ago (mya), primates called Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed. They differed because:
options: Dryopithecus was more ape-like with hairy body, while Ramapithecus was more man-like
Ramapithecus was more ape-like and Dryopithecus walked completely erect
Dryopithecus lived in grasslands and Ramapithecus lived on trees only
Ramapithecus had a cranial capacity of $1400\text{ cc}$
questions.solution: About 15 mya, primates named Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus were existing. They were hairy and walked like gorillas and chimpanzees. Dryopithecus was more ape-like, while Ramapithecus was more man-like.

questions.question: The first human-like hominid ancestor called the 'handy man' or 'tool maker' who had a cranial capacity of $650 - 800\text{ cc}$ was:
questions.solution: The first human-like being the hominid was called Homo habilis. The brain capacities were between $650–800\text{ cc}$. They probably did not eat meat.

questions.question: Pre-historic cave art was developed by Homo sapiens around:
questions.solution: Pre-historic cave art developed about 18,000 years ago (e.g., Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh). Agriculture came around 10,000 years ago.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Fossils are the preserved remains of hard parts of life-forms found in rocks (sedimentary strata).
Statement II: Karl Ernst von Baer noted that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals, thereby disproving Haeckel's biogenetic law.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Paleontological evidence rests on sedimentary rock fossils. Karl Ernst von Baer observed that embryos never pass through adult stages of other species, disproving Ernst Haeckel's biogenetic law.

questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT disturb the Hardy-Weinberg genetic equilibrium?
options: Random mating in a large population
questions.solution: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is maintained by random mating in a large population without mutation, migration, drift, or natural selection. The five factors that disturb equilibrium are: (1) Gene migration/gene flow, (2) Genetic drift, (3) Mutation, (4) Genetic recombination, and (5) Natural selection.

questions.question: The two key concepts of Darwinian theory of evolution are:
questions.solution: Branching descent (phylogeny) and natural selection are the two core fundamental concepts of Darwin's Theory of Evolution.

questions.question: Alfred Russel Wallace, a naturalist who independently conceived the theory of natural selection around the same time as Darwin, worked in:
questions.solution: Alfred Russel Wallace, a contemporary naturalist, worked in the Malay Archipelago and arrived at conclusions similar to Darwin's theory of natural selection.

questions.question: During his voyage on HMS Beagle, Darwin observed different varieties of finches on the Galápagos Islands. From the original seed-eating ancestor, finches evolved diverse beak shapes adapted for eating:
options: Insects, cacti, and vegetation (herbivorous and insectivorous beaks)
questions.solution: From the original seed-eating features, many other forms with altered beaks arose, enabling them to become insectivorous, vegetarian, cactus-feeding, and wood-pecking finches through adaptive radiation.

questions.question: Flippers of Penguins (birds) and Dolphins (mammals) are an example of:
options: Analogous organs evolved due to convergent evolution
Homologous organs evolved due to divergent evolution
questions.solution: Flippers of penguins and dolphins perform the same hydrodynamic swimming function but have different ancestral origins and anatomies, serving as an example of analogous organs resulting from convergent evolution.

questions.question: The first cellular forms of life appeared on Earth approximately:
options: 2000 million years ago (2 billion years ago)
questions.solution: The first cellular forms of life appeared on earth about 2000 million years ago (mya), having evolved from earlier non-cellular macro-aggregates (capsules of RNA, proteins, polysaccharides).

questions.question: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed the theory of evolution based on:
options: Use and disuse of organs and inheritance of acquired characters (e.g., elongation of neck in giraffe)
Natural selection acting on random mutations
Survival of the fittest via differential reproduction
questions.solution: French naturalist Lamarck proposed that evolution of life-forms occurred driven by use and disuse of organs (e.g., giraffes elongated their necks to forage on tall trees, passing on the acquired character).

questions.question: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed the next stage of human evolution called Homo erectus about 1.5 mya. Homo erectus had a cranial capacity of approximately:
questions.solution: Homo erectus fossils discovered in Java in 1891 showed a cranial capacity around $900\text{ cc}$. They lived around 1.5 mya and ate meat.

questions.question: Modern Homo sapiens arose during the ice age between:
options: 75,000 to 10,000 years ago in Africa and spread across continents
questions.solution: During the ice age between 75,000–10,000 years ago, modern Homo sapiens arose in Africa and migrated across continents, developing distinct human races.

questions.question: Embryological support for evolution proposed by Ernst Haeckel was based on the observation that:
options: All vertebrate embryos (including humans) develop vestigial gill slits behind the head, which are functional only in fish
All embryos possess wings at the 4-week stage
Human embryos have functioning gills and scales throughout pregnancy
Embryos do not share any common stages
questions.solution: Embryological support proposed by Ernst Haeckel noted that all vertebrate embryos pass through common developmental stages (e.g., presence of vestigial pharyngeal gill slits in all embryos), which are absent in adult terrestrial vertebrates.

questions.question: Which of the following is a living fossil among vertebrates that represents an ancient crossopterygian lineage connecting fishes to amphibians?
questions.solution: Latimeria (the Coelacanth) is a living lobefin fish that represents the transitional crossopterygian ancestry between aquatic fishes and the first land-dwelling amphibians.

questions.question: In a population of 1000 individuals, 360 belong to genotype $AA$, 480 to $Aa$, and 160 to $aa$. What is the allele frequency of allele '$A$' in this gene pool?
questions.solution: Total alleles $= 1000 \times 2 = 2000$. Alleles for '$A$' $= (360 \times 2) + 480 = 720 + 480 = 1200$. Frequency of allele $A = p = \frac{1200}{2000} = 0.6$.

questions.question: The Neanderthal man with a brain size of $1400\text{ cc}$ lived in near East and Central Asia between:
questions.solution: The Neanderthal man with a brain size of $1400\text{ cc}$ lived in near east and central Asia between 100,000–40,000 years ago. They used animal hides to protect their body and buried their dead.

questions.question: Convergent evolution of two different evolutionary lines (e.g., Placental mammals and Australian marsupials) inhabiting similar ecological niches produces:
options: Analogous structures and functional ecological equivalents
Complete genetic identity between both species
questions.solution: When more than one adaptive radiation occurs in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), it results in convergent evolution, giving rise to analogous organs and ecological equivalents (e.g., Placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf).

questions.question: Which of the following geological eras is known as the 'Age of Reptiles'?
questions.solution: The Mesozoic Era (comprising Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods) is widely recognized as the 'Age of Reptiles' and dinosaurs. The Cenozoic Era is the 'Age of Mammals and Birds'.

questions.question: The Big Bang theory attempts to explain the origin of:
options: The Earth only (4.5 billion years ago)
questions.solution: The Big Bang theory attempts to explain the origin of the universe, postulating a singular huge explosion of dense matter about 20 billion years ago.

questions.question: Earth was formed approximately ________ billion years ago, and life appeared approximately ________ million years after the formation of Earth:
questions.solution: The Earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago. Life appeared 500 million years after the formation of earth, i.e., almost 4 billion years ago.

questions.question: Natural selection in which more individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve is called:
questions.solution: Disruptive selection favours individuals at both extremes of the phenotypic range over intermediate phenotypes, resulting in two distinct peaks in the distribution curve.

questions.question: The idea that life originated on Earth from non-living decaying and rotting matter like straw, mud, etc., was known as the theory of:
questions.solution: For a long time it was believed that life came out of decaying and rotting matter like straw, mud, etc. This was the theory of spontaneous generation (abiogenesis), which was disproved by Louis Pasteur.

questions.question: Which of the following extinct reptiles was a fish-like reptile that evolved around 200 million years ago?
questions.solution: Around 200 mya, some land reptiles moved back into water to evolve into fish-like aquatic reptiles called Ichthyosaurs.

questions.question: Genetic drift operates ONLY in:
options: Small isolated populations due to random chance events
questions.solution: Genetic drift refers to random fluctuations in allele frequencies from generation to generation purely due to chance events. Its effects are pronounced and significant only in small isolated populations.

questions.question: According to Darwinian evolutionary principles, fitness is ultimately measured as:
options: Reproductive fitness (number of fertile offspring contributed to next generation)
questions.solution: Darwinian fitness refers ultimately to reproductive fitness. Individuals with advantageous heritable traits leave more progeny (higher fecundity and survival of offspring) than others.

questions.question: Similarities in proteins and genes (like Cytochrome c amino acid sequence and ribosomal RNA) performing the same function across diverse organisms illustrate:
questions.solution: Similarities in biochemical composition, metabolic pathways, and macromolecules (like DNA, RNA, Cytochrome c) across diverse taxa provide biochemical/molecular homology indicating common evolutionary ancestry.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Human Evolution:
Statement I: Australopithecines lived in East African grasslands about 2 mya and hunted with stone weapons, but essentially ate fruit.
Statement II: Homo erectus had a large brain of around $900\text{ cc}$ and probably ate meat.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Australopithecus lived ~2 mya in East Africa, made simple stone tools, and ate fruits. Homo erectus (~1.5 mya) had a cranial capacity of ~900 cc and was carnivorous.
